requirements.desc: When worktree-mode finalize-cleanup removes a worktree, it must first attempt the existing normal `git worktree remove <path>` path before any force retry.
requirements.note: R1: normal worktree remove is attempted before submodule force retry

requirements.desc: When the normal remove failure is submodule-related, finalize-cleanup must inspect dirty state for the worktree root and initialized submodules before deciding whether to force-remove.
requirements.note: R2: submodule cleanup inspects root and submodule cleanliness

requirements.desc: When the submodule-related failure is confirmed clean, finalize-cleanup must retry `git worktree remove --force <path>` once and continue the existing branch delete and teardown validation path only if that retry succeeds.
requirements.note: R3: clean submodule force retry succeeds before branch deletion

requirements.desc: When the worktree root or any initialized submodule is dirty, finalize-cleanup must keep the worktree and feature branch and return `SUBMODULE_WORKTREE_DIRTY` with bounded dirty path details and recovery guidance.
requirements.note: R4: dirty root or submodule returns SUBMODULE_WORKTREE_DIRTY and preserves resources

requirements.desc: Non-submodule worktree remove failures must retain the existing `WORKTREE_REMOVE_FAILED` behavior and guidance.
requirements.note: R5: non-submodule remove failure retains WORKTREE_REMOVE_FAILED

requirements.desc: The change must preserve existing teardown side effects: report attachment, last-finalized pointer, active-flow clear, branch delete, and validateTeardown execution for successful cleanup.
requirements.note: R6: successful cleanup preserves side effects and teardown validation ordering

requirements.desc: When cleanliness cannot be confirmed, finalize-cleanup must keep the worktree and feature branch and return `SUBMODULE_WORKTREE_STATUS_FAILED` with bounded status failure details and recovery guidance.
requirements.note: R7: status inspection failure returns SUBMODULE_WORKTREE_STATUS_FAILED and preserves resources

requirements.desc: When the clean-confirmed `git worktree remove --force <path>` retry fails, finalize-cleanup must keep the feature branch, report the git failure via `SUBMODULE_WORKTREE_FORCE_REMOVE_FAILED`, and must not run branch deletion.
requirements.note: R8: force retry failure returns SUBMODULE_WORKTREE_FORCE_REMOVE_FAILED before branch deletion

requirements.desc: Diagnostics for dirty, status-failed, or force-remove-failed submodule cleanup must be bounded and must not silently discard git errors.
requirements.note: R9: submodule halt diagnostics are bounded and carry git error output
